name: Op Art
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference, not a style directly named in the source collection. Repeated stripes, checkerboards, concentric circles and geometry create optical illusions through controlled line weight, density and positive-negative balance. A kaleidoscope alone does not establish the style.
suitableUses: Explicitly fits illusion-led pieces. Inferred: psychedelic or demoscene imagery, abstract spatial passages, and key art. The optional poster hybrid suits exhibition, album and event graphics when a title must coexist with an illusion field.
limitations: Keep text outside strong illusion zones; avoid high-frequency flicker. Adapt or omit for dense text during motion, unplanned hidden resets, or topics requiring stable orientation or reduced motion. A vortex must convey a meaningful passage, not just a decorative spiral.
palette: Suggested palette for new artwork only: opaque white background (#FFFFFF) and black foreground (#000000), a discrete two-color monochrome pair. Preserve supplied or approved colors, role assignments, artwork and color-family limits. No gradient or added accent hues; use hatching, patterns or suitable opacity for tone. Check contrast on composited frames; the 21:1 pair alone does not ensure legibility over imagery.
motionAndInteraction: Parametric repeated geometry; animate phase, spacing and deformation at continuous, measured speeds. Drive from shared, seekable time and inspect moiré at final size. Preserve reading holds and deliberate cuts; avoid flicker. Optional chapter passages can use expanding vortex bands and destination reveal, or bounded reversible scene handoffs. For interactive HTML, finite scroll progress may control these states; support pause and reduced motion where applicable. Do not let live input drive video.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied choices. Synchronize to picture, leave speech intelligible and avoid clipping or competing vocals.
assetRequirements: No mandatory assets specified. Generate geometry parametrically. Reuse suitable supplied artwork, exact copy, fonts and authorized audio; preserve asset colors. Prepare and cache stateful simulations where needed. Distinguish simulated appearance from photographed production.
combinations: Best alone for illusion-led work. Optional motion-poster hybrid with style-103: reserve a solid black or white text panel outside the field, keep strictly monochrome, move stripes slowly at constant speed, and match loop endpoints. Avoid text over stripes, flicker and loop jumps. Other pairings unspecified.
productionApproach: Canvas 2D is the recommended renderer; WebGL/GLSL is an alternative. GSAP can own seekable motion, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames handles video composition, timing, synchronization, validation and export; Remotion is fallback only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with reason recorded. These tools do not replace style rendering or motion design. For HTML, use deterministic time-driven rendering; interactive scroll is an optional adapter.
